evidence.quote: Appendix 3: Adverse Events: Definitions and Procedures for Recording, Evaluating, Follow-Up, and Reporting

An AE is any untoward medical occurrence in a patient or clinical study participant, temporally associated with the use of study intervention, whether or not considered related to the study intervention.
All AEs will be collected from the signing of the ICF for the master protocol until participation in an ISA or the master protocol has ended, whichever is longest.

Acetaminophen is the ONLY allowed rescue medication.

abbreviations.definition: adverse event: Any untoward medical occurrence in a patient or clinical investigation subject administered a pharmaceutical product that does not necessarily have a causal relationship with this treatment. An adverse event can therefore be any unfavorable and unintended sign (including an abnormal laboratory finding), symptom, or disease temporally associated with the use of a medicinal (investigational) intervention, whether or not related to the medicinal (investigational) intervention.

A double-blind study is one in which neither the participant nor any of the investigator or sponsor staff who are involved in the treatment or clinical evaluation of the participants are aware of the treatment received.
Columbia Classification Algorithm of Suicide Assessment
Council for International Organizations of Medical Sciences

A complaint is any written, electronic, or oral communication that alleges deficiencies related to the identity, quality, purity, durability, reliability, safety or effectiveness, or performance of a drug or drug delivery system.
Adherence to all study-related, good clinical practice (GCP), and applicable regulatory requirements.
The act of assigning a participant to a treatment. Participants who are enrolled in the study are those who have been assigned to a treatment.
Participants entered into a study are those who sign the informed consent form directly or through their legally acceptable representatives.
Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act
Initiative on Methods, Measurement, and Pain Assessment in Clinical Trials

A process by which a participant voluntarily confirms his or her willingness to participate in a particular study, after having been informed of all aspects of the study that are relevant to the participant’s decision to participate. Informed consent is documented by means of a written, signed, and dated informed consent form.
An interim analysis is an analysis of clinical study data, separated into treatment groups, that is conducted before the final reporting database is created/locked.

A pharmaceutical form of an active ingredient or placebo being tested or used as a reference in a clinical trial, including products already on the market when used or assembled (formulated or packaged) in a way that is different from the authorized form, or marketed products used for an unauthorized indication, or marketed products used to gain further information about the authorized form.

intention to treat: The principle that asserts that the effect of a treatment policy can be best assessed by evaluating on the basis of the intention to treat a participant (that is, the planned treatment regimen) rather than the actual treatment given. It has the consequence that participants allocated to a treatment group should be followed up, assessed, and analyzed as members of that group irrespective of their compliance to the planned course of treatment.
Equivalent to CDISC term ‘subject’: an individual who participates in a clinical trial, either as a recipient of an investigational medicinal product or as a control.
QT interval corrected for heart rate using Fridericia’s formula
The act of determining if an individual meets minimum requirements to become part of a pool of potential candidates for participation in a clinical study.

treatment-emergent adverse event: An untoward medical occurrence that emerges during a defined treatment period, having been absent pretreatment, or worsens relative to the pretreatment state, and does not necessarily have to have a causal relationship with this treatment.

instruments.name: Visual Analog Scale
instruments.scoring_or_range: 0 to 100: 0 = no pain, and 100 = worst imaginable pain

evidence.quote: Pain intensity Visual Analog Scale (VAS)* for pain

The VAS for pain will be used at screening and at each clinic visit. This is a graphic, single-item scale where participants are asked to describe their pain intensity over the past week, in the area under study, on a scale of 0 to 100: 0 = no pain, and 100 = worst imaginable pain.
Participants complete the VAS by placing a line perpendicular to the VAS line at a point that describes their pain intensity.
have a visual analog scale (VAS) pain value >40 and <95 at Visits 1 and 2
V2 procedure should be repeated if >60 days from V1

instruments.name: Numeric Rating Scale
instruments.scoring_or_range: 0 to 10: 0 = no pain, and 10 = pain as bad as you can imagine
instruments.purpose: Pain intensity; primary efficacy outcome measure (average pain); secondary measure (worst pain)

evidence.quote: The NRS will be used during the PDEP and daily throughout the study to describe pain severity. This is a numeric, single-item scale where participants are asked to describe their average and worst pain over the past 24 hours, on a scale of 0 to 10: 0 = no pain, and 10 = pain as bad as you can imagine.
Participants complete the NRS daily using a take-home device.
‘Please rate your pain by selecting the one number [0-10] that describes your AVERAGE level of [area under study] pain during the past 24 hours.’
‘Please rate your pain by selecting the one number [0-10] that describes your WORST level of [area under study] pain during the past 24 hours.’
Collected daily with a take-home device. Compliance reviewed at each clinic visit.
7-day minimum NRS data and rescue use medication collected daily at home post washout and prior to randomization.

instruments.name: Patient Global Impression of Change
instruments.mode: either an electronic device or on paper
instruments.scoring_or_range: 1 to 7: 1 = very much better, and 7 = very much worse

evidence.quote: Participant ratings of overall improvement Patient Global Impression of Change (PGI)*

The Patient Global Impression of Change (PGI) is used across all disease states. It captures the participant’s perspective of treatment apart from sub-aspects of the general improvement. This is a numeric scale from 1 to 7: 1 = very much better, and 7 = very much worse.
‘Mark the box that best describes how your pain symptoms are now, compared to how they were before you started taking this medicine.’
Self-reported questionnaires will be administered by either an electronic device or on paper.

instruments.name: EuroQol-5D 5 level questionnaire
instruments.mode: either an electronic device or on paper
instruments.scoring_or_range: 5 dimensions, 5 options under each dimension; health profile or single summary index number; EQ VAS 0 to 100: 0 = the worst health you can imagine, and 100 = the best health you can imagine

evidence.quote: Emotional functioning EuroQol-5D 5 level questionnaire (EQ-5D-5L)*
The EQ-5D-5L health status questionnaire is used across all disease states.
The EQ-5D-5L is one of the most popular patient-completed instruments to address quality of life (Buchholz et. al. 2018).

The participant is asked to ‘check the ONE box that best describes your health TODAY,’ choosing from 5 options provided under each dimension. The scores on the 5 dimensions can be presented as a health profile or converted to a single summary index number.

The EQ-5D-5L also includes the EQ VAS, which records the participant’s self-rated health on a vertical VAS of 0 to 100: 0 = the worst health you can imagine, and 100 = the best health you can imagine.
Self-reported questionnaires will be administered by either an electronic device or on paper.

instruments.name: Medical Outcomes Study (MOS) Sleep Scale
instruments.mode: either an electronic device or on paper
instruments.scoring_or_range: 12 questions; 5-point categorical scale ranging from ‘all of the time’ to ‘none of the time.’; quantity of sleep reported as the average number of hours slept each night

evidence.quote: Quality of sleep Medical Outcomes Study (MOS) Sleep Scale*

This scale consists of 12 questions addressing the past week. Participants report how often each sleep symptom or problem is present on a 5-point categorical scale ranging from ‘all of the time’ to ‘none of the time.’ The question about time to fall asleep is reported by a 5-point categorical scale and the quantity of sleep is reported as the average number of hours slept each night.
MOS Sleep Scale multi-item scores of sleep disturbance, somnolence, sleep adequacy, and the sleep problems index.
Self-reported questionnaires will be administered by either an electronic device or on paper.

evidence.quote: At V1, use the C-SSRS Baseline version. All subsequent assessments will use the C-SSRS Since Last Visit version.

notes: Version (rule 11): the PDF holds a single protocol version, H0P-MC-CPMP Amendment (a) (approval 11-Dec-2020; original protocol 30 January 2020 is not in the PDF); the SoA (pages 17-23) and all extractions are from amendment (a). The Protocol Amendment Summary of Changes Table (pages 4-8) describes what (a) changed relative to the original; it is quoted where it is the only text on an activity (B12/methylmalonic acid/homocysteine added for Visit 1; recreational drug use 'For screening purposes'; Self-Pain Positioning Questionnaire 'Part of the digital biomarkers analysis'; respiratory rate added to vital signs notes per FDA feedback; ECG position changed from sitting to supine; Pharmacogenetic and Exploratory Biomarker Sample Collection table changed plasma to whole blood). Conflicts recorded (rule 5): (1) Vital signs - SoA note lists pulse rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure and temperature; Section 8.2.2 lists blood pressure, pulse rate, body temperature (no respiratory rate); both recorded as separate measurements entries. (2) Pregnancy - SoA row is 'Serum pregnancy', the lab-tests table lists 'Pregnancy test (serum, urine)'. (3) Abbreviation wording differs between lists: PGI = 'Patient Global Impression of Change' (p23) vs 'Patient’s Global Impression of Change' (p90); TSH 'thyroid stimulating hormone' (p23) vs 'thyroid-stimulating hormone' (p75); HbA1c (p23) vs HbA1C (p75); lab table defines 'HDL' while the table prints HDL-C; Appendix 7 prints 'MCRP' for magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography while the body (p50) uses MRCP; body p46 says 'Medical Outcome Study (MOS)'. Rule 10: the lab-tests table on page 75 runs its columns together in the text layer; it was read from the PDF page image (page_75.png) before assigning analytes. The image confirms 5 columns (Chemistry; Hematology and Differential; Urinalysis; Urine Drug Screen; Other Tests) and that 'Lipid Panel' (HDL-C, LDL-C) is a bold sub-heading inside the Chemistry column after B12/Methylmalonic acid/Homocysteine, while Cholesterol and Triglycerides sit in Chemistry itself; Other Tests holds 'Hormones (female)' (Pregnancy test (serum, urine), FSH, Estradiol, TSH) and 'Other' (HbA1C, HIV). Page 22 (last SoA page, spaced text layer) was also checked as an image; it confirms the row/note assignment and shows the 'Participant Device' row content is redacted (CCI). Page 76 was checked as an image: fully redacted (CCI), presumably the Pharmacogenetic and Exploratory Biomarker Sample Collection table referred to on page 8. No page lacks a text layer, so no entries are marked read_from page image. Several pages have a letter-spaced text layer (e.g. 2, 4-5, 7, 14, 22, 27, 29, 37-38, 54-56, 71, 73); quotes from them keep that spacing. Panels: the Appendix 6 hepatic evaluation tests (pages 85-87; central testing except microbiology, which is local only) are event-driven, not SoA rows, and are recorded as panels prefixed 'Hepatic Evaluation Testing:'. Lab for SoA lab activities is the central laboratory per Appendix 2 (p74), which also allows sponsor-approved local laboratory testing in lieu of central testing. No specimen is stated for hematology, chemistry, lipid panel, urinalysis, hormones, HbA1c or HIV. Redacted (CCI) content: Sections 8.7 Genetics and 8.8 Biomarkers (pages 54-55), Appendix 5 Genetics (page 84), page 76, and the 'Participant Device' SoA row (page 22). Hence nothing beyond the amendment-summary line is available for Exploratory biomarker samples and Pharmacogenetic sample (specimen 'whole blood' rests on page 8 only, and the summary does not say which of the two samples it applies to - recorded for both). SoA rows the text does not describe beyond the SoA: Informed consent for master protocol / for ISA (only Section 10.1.3 generic process), Evaluate master protocol I/E criteria, Pain medication washout (Design Outline only), Medical history, Family history, Demographics (SoA note only: age, gender, race, ethnicity), Height (no text; BMI <40 kg/m2 in inclusion criterion [4]), AEs and Preexisting conditions (Section 8.3/10.3), Concomitant medications (Section 6.5), Rescue medication usage reporting (Section 6.5 via cross-reference), Alcohol consumption (only Section 5.3 intake limits; amendment rationale 'Medical decision'), Recreational drug use (only amendment summary), Self-pain positioning questionnaire (only amendment summary; no description of content, respondent or mode), Participant Device (row content redacted). Pain catastrophizing scale is named only in inclusion criterion [3] (≤30); no description, version or abbreviation. Instrument versions are null except C-SSRS (Baseline / Since Last Visit, adapted) and EQ-5D-5L ('used in its EQ-5D-5L version'). Undefined tokens in SoA activity names: 'B12' is not defined in any abbreviation list. All other tokens (I/E, PDEP, ECG, AEs, VAS, NRS, PGI, EQ-5D-5L, MOS, C-SSRS, FSH, TSH, HbA1c, HIV, ISA) are defined (p23 SoA abbreviations and/or Appendix 7).
